Shanghai/Ningbo.note: eventEnded is cleared back to null this run. It had been set to 2026-08-30 on the assumption Saudel had stopped being a factor, and that call was wrong: JMA has Saudel active again as a named tropical storm, and SEKO's 1 Sep update has waiting times deteriorating rather than clearing — Shanghai from 6-11 to 7-10+ days, Ningbo now past 10 days, Yangshan yard density 85-88%, Meishan 95%, reefer plugs 94%. remarks: Nothing is suspended. Saudel is a tropical storm again after its 28 Aug Zhejiang landfall and is crossing the northern South China Sea, but it is forecast to weaken to a depression as it curls back toward the Pearl River Delta, and no terminal or carrier has announced a closure for this phase.

Yantian is the one to watch: JMA's track brings Saudel within roughly 88 km on about 5 Sep. The queue there is currently small, so a short closure would be absorbable — the concern is a second South China disruption landing while East China is still 10 days deep in backlog.

The real story is still Shanghai/Ningbo, and it is getting worse rather than better. SEKO's 1 Sep update puts Ningbo waits above 10 days and Shanghai at 7-10+, against Linerlytica's 1.68M TEU at anchorage and a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.24 on 30 Aug.

A second named system, Krovanh (TC2628), is nearly stationary south of Japan and drifting toward the Amami islands. Its closest forecast approach to a tracked port is about 670 km from Shanghai/Ningbo and 725 km from Busan, both outside the 600 km threshold, so it is left out of the incoming table.
Qingdao (1.5-2 days), Busan (1.5-2 days) and Singapore (1-1.5 days) are all reported at normal-to-mild delay levels with no weather event attached, so they are omitted rather than listed as open.
